scope: Evidence for seven exact city identities and naming chronologies; no checkout files edited.
semantics: Name periods are Gregorian civil-date evidence, with inclusive endpoints. A null initial start records an unresearched beginning of the first name, not evidence of existence before a city was founded. Implementation must additionally require valid source observations/tenure.

For a population record, the historical display name must correspond to its actual observation date/year. A selected map year may be different; no source observation may be presented as an observation in that selected year.

If only an annual observation is known and a name changes within that same year, do not silently assign a precise civil date to the observation. Use a documented annual display convention or show both names; these current population rows have no transition-year ambiguity.
Modern-reference cities stay modern. They are identity-check references here, not evidence that modern names belong to historical years.
Chinese names are editorial Simplified Chinese display translations. They do not add identity equivalence, political sovereignty, population scope or founding dates.

yek-museum.title: History of Russia in Photographs / Multimedia Art Museum exhibition
yek-museum.evidenceSummary: Exhibition states Yekaterinburg was renamed Sverdlovsk on 14 October 1924 and the historic name returned on 23 September 1991.

yek-archive.title: State Archive of Social and Political History of Sverdlovsk Oblast
yek-archive.type: state archive history using archival holdings
yek-archive.evidenceSummary: Distinguishes local decision on 4 September 1991 from Presidium approval on 23 September. The latter is the display transition.

samara-1935.title: USSR Central Executive Committee decree, 27 January 1935
samara-1935.evidenceSummary: Catalogue describes decree renaming Samara to Kuybyshev dated 27 January 1935, published in Izvestiia No. 23 on 28 January.

samara-1991.title: Samara Regional Library for the Blind — restoration of city name
samara-1991.evidenceSummary: Records restoration to Samara by decree dated 25 January 1991. The paragraph explicitly differentiates the two renamings.

samara-decree.title: RSFSR Presidium decree, 25 January 1991, reproduced by Garant
samara-decree.evidenceSummary: Decree text renames Kuybyshev to Samara; identifies Vedomosti 1991 No. 5, article 59.
samara-decree.access: indexed full decree text retrieved; direct open 403

volgograd.title: Volgograd State University — History of the City
volgograd.evidenceSummary: Explicit dates: Tsaritsyn to Stalingrad on 10 April 1925; Stalingrad to Volgograd on 10 November 1961.

kaliningrad.title: Kaliningrad City Council — regional history
kaliningrad.evidenceSummary: Explicitly dates both Königsberg city and region renaming to Kaliningrad to 4 July 1946. Use only this naming claim; no territorial-status conclusion is imported.

petersburg-library.title: Presidential Library — Saint Petersburg renamed Petrograd
petersburg-library.evidenceSummary: Gives 18 August Julian / 31 August Gregorian 1914 for Petrograd; 26 January 1924 for Leningrad; 6 September 1991 for restored Saint Petersburg.

petersburg-archive.title: Saint Petersburg Archives — City name exhibition
petersburg-archive.evidenceSummary: Primary documentary sequence: 18 August 1914 old style; 26 January 1924 congress resolution; 6 September 1991 decree. Explains local January 23 proposal versus national January 26 approval.
petersburg-archive.access: detailed indexed text retrieved; direct page timed out

petersburg-municipal.title: Saint Petersburg City Administration — cultural statistics
petersburg-municipal.evidenceSummary: Confirms Saint Petersburg 1703–1914, Petrograd 1914–1924, Leningrad 1924–1991 and restoration 6 September 1991.

nizhny-municipal.title: Nizhny Novgorod City Administration — general information
nizhny-municipal.evidenceSummary: Explicit dates: renamed for Gorky from 7 October 1932; historical name returned on 22 October 1990.
nizhny-municipal.access: indexed page retrieved; related municipal document direct open failed

istanbul-municipal.title: Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality — history of the city’s names
istanbul-municipal.evidenceSummary: Lists Constantinople as Byzantine official name and multiple coexisting Ottoman names, including Istanbul. Supports coexistence, not a universal exclusive 1930 renaming date.

istanbul-frus.title: US Office of the Historian — FRUS 1930 Volume III, Turkish negotiations
istanbul-frus.evidenceSummary: Contemporaneous diplomatic document headings use Constantinople on 2 October 1929 and Istanbul on 18 March 1930. This is dated English usage evidence, not a legal city-renaming decree.

istanbul-unesco.title: UNESCO — Historic Areas of Istanbul
istanbul-unesco.evidenceSummary: Existing project rule cites UNESCO for Byzantine Constantinople. Existing exact observation bindings are preserved; this review does not extend their end date or impose a 1930 legal date.
istanbul-unesco.access: existing project citation; not newly fetched this pass

sverdlovsk-ukraine-institution.title: Canadian Institute of Ukrainian Studies — Encyclopedia of Ukraine, Sverdlovsk
sverdlovsk-ukraine-institution.evidenceSummary: Identifies Sverdlovs’k as a Luhansk-oblast city, formed by amalgamation of mining settlements in 1938; gives 2013 population 65,276. This is a different city from Yekaterinburg.

dovzhansk-map.title: Visicom — Dovzhansk (Sverdlovsk)
dovzhansk-map.evidenceSummary: Map provider gives Luhanska oblast location center [39.66152260073741,48.064899508796344], bbox [39.58659861446542,48.00941500982516,39.73561923863272,48.10800581495756]. The Chandler point lies inside this city bbox.

dovzhansk-statistics.title: State Statistics Service of Ukraine — Population on 1 January 2019
dovzhansk-statistics.evidenceSummary: Indexed table distinguishes Dovzhansk city population 63,576 present / 63,358 permanent from city-council aggregate 95,990 / 95,712. These modern values are contextual evidence only, not substitutes for 1950 or 1975.
dovzhansk-statistics.access: indexed table retrieved; direct PDF timed out

population-input.title: Reba, Reitsma & Seto digitization of Chandler urban population
population-input.evidenceSummary: Exact original row is retained locally as chandler:1356: name Sverdlovs'k, coordinates [39.651631,48.08455], countryReference Ukraine, observations 1950=610000 and 1975=1345000. Original Chandler printed pages not located in this pass.

kaliningrad-rosstat.title: Kaliningrad regional office of Rosstat — History of regional statistics
kaliningrad-rosstat.evidenceSummary: Confirms by USSR Presidium decrees that Königsberg city became Kaliningrad on 4 July 1946.

quarantineCandidates.action: Exclude this exact row from historical map population display and country-dossier spatial association pending identity review; preserve the source row and values in downloadable data. Do not migrate its coordinates or attach Q887.
facts: Source-derived coordinates and Ukraine countryReference point to the Luhansk Sverdlovsk/Dovzhansk, not the Urals city.
The record point lies inside the first-party Visicom Dovzhansk city bbox.
Its distance to the separate Yekaterinburg source point is 1709.7 km.
An institutional Ukrainian encyclopedia identifies this city as formed in 1938 and having 65,276 inhabitants in 2013; this is distinct from the Yekaterinburg identity.

That intended population-city identity is NOT proven without the original Chandler pages or an upstream correction. Population magnitude alone cannot establish it.
